groups.title: Eloquent ORM Core
groups.question: A user changes their role to admin by adding a field to the profile form, and your orders page runs hundreds of queries. Explain how Eloquent handles both.

followUps.Mass Assignment and the fillable/guarded: How do $fillable and $guarded stop users from setting fields they should not?
followUps.Eloquent Relationships and Lazy vs Eager: What is the N+1 problem and how does eager loading fix it?

evidence.text: Mass assignment fills many attributes from request data at once.
$fillable lists the fields that may be mass-assigned.
Without it, a user could set fields like is_admin by adding them to the form.
Accessing a relationship in a loop runs a new query for each item.
Eager loading with with() loads the relationship for all items in one extra query.
Laravel can be set to throw on lazy loading in development to catch this.

notEnough: Only saying eager loading is faster.

groups.title: Database Migrations
groups.question: A rollback broke your database because a migration's down method did not undo its up method, and order lookups by customer are slow. Explain how migrations and indexes should be written.

followUps.Migration Versioning and the up/down Con: Why must down() reverse up() exactly?
followUps.Column Modifiers and Index Strategy: How do column modifiers and indexes affect the schema and performance?

evidence.text: Migrations are versioned changes applied in order.
down() must undo exactly what up() did.
Otherwise rolling back leaves the database broken or inconsistent.

notEnough: Only saying migrations have up and down.

evidence.text: Modifiers like nullable, default and unsigned define column rules.
Indexes on foreign keys and filtered columns speed up lookups.
A missing index makes queries scan the whole table as data grows.

notEnough: Only saying indexes make queries faster.

groups.title: Query Builder and Raw Queries
groups.question: You need to update 100,000 rows in a batch job and a report uses a complex query with user input. Explain when you would use the query builder and how you stay safe from SQL injection.

followUps.Query Builder vs Eloquent Trade-offs: When is the query builder better than Eloquent?
followUps.Preventing SQL Injection with Parameter: How does parameter binding prevent SQL injection, and where can you lose it?

evidence.text: The query builder returns plain results and is faster for bulk work.
Eloquent returns model objects with events, casts and relationships.
Bulk updates through the builder skip model events, which may matter.

notEnough: Only saying the builder is faster.

evidence.text: The query builder and Eloquent send values separately from the SQL.
User input is treated as data, never as SQL.
Raw methods that concatenate user input into SQL lose that protection.

notEnough: Only saying Laravel prevents SQL injection.

groups.title: Database Seeders and Factories
groups.question: Your tests depend on records someone created by hand, and new developers start with an empty database. Explain how factories and seeders fix this.

followUps.Model Factories for Realistic Test Data: How do model factories help tests?
followUps.Seeders and Environment-Specific Data: Why separate seeders for reference data and development data?

evidence.text: Factories generate realistic fake data for each model.
Each test creates exactly the records it needs.
Factory states create variations, like an unverified user.
Some data, like roles and permissions, is needed in every environment.
Sample data is only for development and must not reach production.
Splitting seeders lets each environment run only what it needs.

notEnough: Only saying seeders fill the database.
